evidence: PATHS: instruction.md:11 names /instructions/hireops_rules.md and /instructions/integration.md; instruction.md:13 names /assets/seed_data.json; hireops_rules.md:205 names /assets/seed_data.json. All three exist under task/environment/ (assets/seed_data.json, instructions/hireops_rules.md, instructions/integration.md). task/environment/Dockerfile:14-16 'COPY instructions/ /instructions/', 'COPY assets/ /assets/', 'chmod -R a+rX /instructions /assets' (byte-identical to the frozen template Dockerfile). Template's placeholder notes.md is replaced by task-specific hireops_rules.md (task-specific, allowed); integration.md differs from template only by the appended delivery/symlink paragraph, which matches test.sh symlink policy (test.sh identical to template). CONTENT vs PROMPT/RULES: seed_data.json parses; keys stages(6), candidate_status_labels, thread_page_size=30, users(10), jobs(3), applications(16), messages(127), notes(3), reads(6). Users/emails/roles match instruction.md:17 and app_context.md:10-19 exactly (3 recruiters, 3 hiring managers, 1 observer, 3 candidates). Rules s9 claims (three jobs with ordered cards, one long conversation, a few notes, read markers as counts from first message, candidate wording and page size 30 in the file) all hold; candidate_status_labels equal the table at hireops_rules.md:182-189. Seed is self-consistent with rules: per job/stage positions contiguous from 1; Interview occupancy 2/3, 1/2, 1/3 within interview_limit (1-50); no duplicate email per job; rejected APP-301 carries rejected_from SCREEN and non-blank reason; messages chronological. CONTENT vs JUDGES: app_context.md:29-30 'three jobs; Noor Haddad's Platform Engineer conversation is long (120 messages at the start)' -> APP-101 has exactly 120 messages, Noor (USR-CAN1) on JOB-PLAT 'Platform Engineer'. functional/prompt.md:25 'Lena ... Product Designer conversation; the starting read markers give her 1' -> APP-301 on JOB-DSGN 'Product Designer', 3 messages (REC3, CAN3, REC3), Lena read_count 2, third message is staff -> 1 unread; no other judge (polish/visual/gates grep) signs in as Lena, and Z runs first. functional T/U/K reference Tomas's Data Analyst conversation (APP-201 on JOB-DATA) and Ingrid/Bill as J1/J2 managers (seeded hiring_manager accounts) - consistent. Judges otherwise build their own jobs/cards and explicitly 'never rely on starting counts'. CONTENT vs SOLUTION: solution/app/src/seed_data.json is byte-identical to environment/assets/seed_data.json (both sha256 a1c65c80...7740); db.js:10 loads it via __dirname (copied into /app by solve.sh 'cp -a app/. /app/', so no runtime /assets dependency, consistent with instruction.md:15); db.js:13-15,66-84 consumes stages, candidate_status_labels, thread_page_size, users, jobs, applications (incl. rejected_from/reject_reason/position), messages, reads (read_count -> last_read_id of message read_count-1, matching rules s9 semantics) and notes. RUN EVIDENCE: raw-evidence-index.json artifacts (workspace.cjs, results/workspace.json, server.log, pngs) all re-hash correctly and record solution/app/src/seed_data.json with a hash matching the frozen bytes; results/workspace.json reports 'thread paging 30 at a time' and unread/seen checks passed under the scripted golden (not a configured judge run). ADVERSARIAL: a broken app that ignores read markers (all counts 0) is caught by functional Z (Lena expects 1); an app that seeds only users but not messages fails T (Noor's 30-of-120) and visual. A conforming alternative that treats read_count as message count (as rules define) gets Lena=1 and Noor=0 unread, matching the judges; I found no seed fact the judges assume that a spec-following app could legitimately derive differently. No mismatch found.
